title.narrative: VRI Bhamo, Kachin State

description.narrative: This indicator is the score of the VRI conducted in Bhamo, Kachin State. Progress against these indicators will be measured using a Vulnerability and Resilience Assessment Methodology. This innovative methodology will be developed and tested in the initial year of NRM.

comment.narrative: The VRI is a composite measure composed of a broad basket of indicators grouped into three categories which is designed to enable updated crosscomparison and vulnerability tracking despite inconsistent and often out of date data availability. The VRI process is multistage engaging both IPs and communities in the setting of an initial score. First the CAR conducts a review of available secondary data seeking out information which speaks to any of the listed indicators. Next the list of indicators is reviewed for gaps if any of the three categories noted above are too sparsely populated with secondary data points additional primary research is carried out by Community Listeners qualitative researchers and community members selected from the programming areas. The number of Community Listeners per township is dependent on the demographic characteristics of the township and is aimed at providing full coverage of different ethnic or religious communities. Generally primary data collection is limited to 10 key informant interviews KIIs per Township per Community Listener using purposive sampling to ensure adequate demographic diversity of participants. Responses are cleaned translated from local languages to English and analysed at which point they can be made to serve as indicator data points or supplementary data to existing data points.

Given the significant deterioration of the context across all regions and states of Myanmar the NRM aims to maintain the scores identified at the baseline in other words we want to at least try to make sure things do not get worse in the township which is a major challenge given the ongoing conflict and crisis. A change in circumstances may allow for the target to be revised.

comment.narrative: The VRI is a composite measure composed of a broad basket of indicators grouped into three categories which is designed to enable updated crosscomparison and vulnerability tracking despite inconsistent and often out of date data availability. The VRI process is multistage engaging both IPs and communities in the setting of an initial score. First the CAR conducts a review of available secondary data seeking out information which speaks to any of the listed indicators. Next the list of indicators is reviewed for gaps if any of the three categories noted above are too sparsely populated with secondary data points additional primary research is carried out by Community Listeners qualitative researchers and community members selected from the programming areas. The number of Community Listeners per township is dependent on the demographic characteristics of the township and is aimed at providing full coverage of different ethnic or religious communities. Generally primary data collection is limited to 10 key informant interviews KIIs per Township per Community Listener using purposive sampling to ensure adequate demographic diversity of participants. Responses are cleaned translated from local languages to English and analysed at which point they can be made to serve as indicator data points or supplementary data to existing data points.

Given the significant deterioration of the context across all regions and states of Myanmar the NRM aims to maintain the scores identified at the baseline in other words we want to at least try to make sure things do not get worse in the township which is a major challenge given the ongoing conflict and crisis. A change in circumstances may allow for the target to be revised.

Vulnerability and Resilience Index will combine measurement of vulnerability focused on exposurerisk by type frequency and intensity of shocks and stressors and measurement of resilience as a adaptive capacity focused on structural factors community capacities and household capacities and b a state focused on a basket of indicators such as food security asset ownership health status etc.. Rights are protected when vulnerabilities are reduced and are also integral to adaptive capacity and resilience.

comment.narrative: The VRI is a composite measure composed of a broad basket of indicators grouped into three categories which is designed to enable updated crosscomparison and vulnerability tracking despite inconsistent and often out of date data availability. The VRI process is multistage engaging both IPs and communities in the setting of an initial score. First the CAR conducts a review of available secondary data seeking out information which speaks to any of the listed indicators. Next the list of indicators is reviewed for gaps if any of the three categories noted above are too sparsely populated with secondary data points additional primary research is carried out by Community Listeners qualitative researchers and community members selected from the programming areas. The number of Community Listeners per township is dependent on the demographic characteristics of the township and is aimed at providing full coverage of different ethnic or religious communities. Generally primary data collection is limited to 10 key informant interviews KIIs per Township per Community Listener using purposive sampling to ensure adequate demographic diversity of participants. Responses are cleaned translated from local languages to English and analysed at which point they can be made to serve as indicator data points or supplementary data to existing data points.

Given the significant deterioration of the context across all regions and states of Myanmar the NRM aims to maintain the scores identified at the baseline in other words we want to at least try to make sure things do not get worse in the township which is a major challenge given the ongoing conflict and crisis. A change in circumstances may allow for the target to be revised.

The VRI process is multistage engaging both IPs and communities in the setting of an initial score. First the CAR conducts a review of available secondary data seeking out information which speaks to any of the listed indicators. Next the list of indicators is reviewed for gaps if any of the three categories noted above are too sparsely populated with secondary data points additional primary research is carried out by Community Listeners qualitative researchers and community members selected from the programming areas. The number of Community Listeners per township is dependent on the demographic characteristics of the township and is aimed at providing full coverage of different ethnic or religious communities. Generally primary data collection is limited to 10 key informant interviews KIIs per Township per Community Listener using purposive sampling to ensure adequate demographic diversity of participants. Responses are cleaned translated from local languages to English and analysed at which point they can be made to serve as indicator data points or supplementary data to existing data points.

Given the significant deterioration of the context across all regions and states of Myanmar the NRM aims to maintain the scores identified at the baseline in other words we want to at least try to make sure things do not get worse in the township which is a major challenge given the ongoing conflict and crisis. A change in circumstances may allow for the target to be revised.

title.narrative: Community selfassessed vulnerability score

description.narrative: Vulnerability is assessed through the use of a Participatory Vulnerability and Resilience Analysis (PVRA) tool, applied to a sample of target communities per partner. The vulnerability component combines community selfassessment (weighted scoring) of the current status around the following key areas into an overall vulnerability status score: Shelter Food security Health Education Shelter WASH

comment.narrative: The VRI is a composite measure composed of a broad basket of indicators grouped into three categories which is designed to enable updated crosscomparison and vulnerability tracking despite inconsistent and often out of date data availability. The VRI process is multistage engaging both IPs and communities in the setting of an initial score. First the CAR conducts a review of available secondary data seeking out information which speaks to any of the listed indicators. Next the list of indicators is reviewed for gaps if any of the three categories noted above are too sparsely populated with secondary data points additional primary research is carried out by Community Listeners qualitative researchers and community members selected from the programming areas. The number of Community Listeners per township is dependent on the demographic characteristics of the township and is aimed at providing full coverage of different ethnic or religious communities. Generally primary data collection is limited to 10 key informant interviews KIIs per Township per Community Listener using purposive sampling to ensure adequate demographic diversity of participants. Responses are cleaned translated from local languages to English and analysed at which point they can be made to serve as indicator data points or supplementary data to existing data points.

Given the significant deterioration of the context across all regions and states of Myanmar the NRM aims to maintain the scores identified at the baseline in other words we want to at least try to make sure things do not get worse in the township which is a major challenge given the ongoing conflict and crisis. A change in circumstances may allow for the target to be revised.

title.narrative: VRI Namtu, Northern Shan State

description.narrative: This indicator is the score of the VRI conducted in Namtu, Northern Shan State. Progress against these indicators will be measured using a Vulnerability and Resilience Assessment Methodology. This innovative methodology will be developed and tested in the initial year of NRM.

comment.narrative: The VRI is a composite measure composed of a broad basket of indicators grouped into three categories which is designed to enable updated crosscomparison and vulnerability tracking despite inconsistent and often out of date data availability. The VRI process is multistage engaging both IPs and communities in the setting of an initial score. First the CAR conducts a review of available secondary data seeking out information which speaks to any of the listed indicators. Next the list of indicators is reviewed for gaps if any of the three categories noted above are too sparsely populated with secondary data points additional primary research is carried out by Community Listeners qualitative researchers and community members selected from the programming areas. The number of Community Listeners per township is dependent on the demographic characteristics of the township and is aimed at providing full coverage of different ethnic or religious communities. Generally primary data collection is limited to 10 key informant interviews KIIs per Township per Community Listener using purposive sampling to ensure adequate demographic diversity of participants. Responses are cleaned translated from local languages to English and analysed at which point they can be made to serve as indicator data points or supplementary data to existing data points

Given the significant deterioration of the context across all regions and states of Myanmar the NRM aims to maintain the scores identified at the baseline in other words we want to at least try to make sure things do not get worse in the township which is a major challenge given the ongoing conflict and crisis. A change in circumstances may allow for the target to be revised.

description.narrative: This indicator is the score of the VRI conducted in Kyaukme, Northern Shan State. Progress against these indicators will be measured using a Vulnerability and Resilience Assessment Methodology. This innovative methodology will be developed and tested in the initial year of NRM.

comment.narrative: The VRI is a composite measure composed of a broad basket of indicators grouped into three categories which is designed to enable updated crosscomparison and vulnerability tracking despite inconsistent and often out of date data availability. The VRI process is multistage engaging both IPs and communities in the setting of an initial score. First the CAR conducts a review of available secondary data seeking out information which speaks to any of the listed indicators. Next the list of indicators is reviewed for gaps if any of the three categories noted above are too sparsely populated with secondary data points additional primary research is carried out by Community Listeners qualitative researchers and community members selected from the programming areas. The number of Community Listeners per township is dependent on the demographic characteristics of the township and is aimed at providing full coverage of different ethnic or religious communities. Generally primary data collection is limited to 10 key informant interviews KIIs per Township per Community Listener using purposive sampling to ensure adequate demographic diversity of participants. Responses are cleaned translated from local languages to English and analysed at which point they can be made to serve as indicator data points or supplementary data to existing data points.

Given the significant deterioration of the context across all regions and states of Myanmar the NRM aims to maintain the scores identified at the baseline in other words we want to at least try to make sure things do not get worse in the township which is a major challenge given the ongoing conflict and crisis. A change in circumstances may allow for the target to be revised.

comment.narrative: The VRI is a composite measure composed of a broad basket of indicators grouped into three categories which is designed to enable updated crosscomparison and vulnerability tracking despite inconsistent and often out of date data availability. The VRI process is multistage engaging both IPs and communities in the setting of an initial score. First the CAR conducts a review of available secondary data seeking out information which speaks to any of the listed indicators. Next the list of indicators is reviewed for gaps if any of the three categories noted above are too sparsely populated with secondary data points additional primary research is carried out by Community Listeners qualitative researchers and community members selected from the programming areas. The number of Community Listeners per township is dependent on the demographic characteristics of the township and is aimed at providing full coverage of different ethnic or religious communities. Generally primary data collection is limited to 10 key informant interviews KIIs per Township per Community Listener using purposive sampling to ensure adequate demographic diversity of participants. Responses are cleaned translated from local languages to English and analysed at which point they can be made to serve as indicator data points or supplementary data to existing data points.

Given the significant deterioration of the context across all regions and states of Myanmar the NRM aims to maintain the scores identified at the baseline in other words we want to at least try to make sure things do not get worse in the township which is a major challenge given the ongoing conflict and crisis. A change in circumstances may allow for the target to be revised.

Responses are cleaned translated from local languages to English and analysed at which point they can be made to serve as indicator data points or supplementary data to existing data points.

Given the significant deterioration of the context across all regions and states of Myanmar the NRM aims to maintain the scores identified at the baseline in other words we want to at least try to make sure things do not get worse in the township which is a major challenge given the ongoing conflict and crisis. A change in circumstances may allow for the target to be revised.

title.narrative: R1. Expansion of sustainable, inclusive and fair livelihood opportunities (SDG 1,8)

description.narrative: R1. Expansion of sustainable, inclusive and fair livelihood opportunities (SDG 1,8)Expansion of sustainable, inclusive and fair livelihood opportunities (SDG 1,8)

title.narrative: R1.1. Number of persons receiving support related to sustainable livelihoods, secure employment, improved working conditions or professional/vocational and life skills

description.narrative: This indicator captures the number of individuals receiving support related to sustainable, inclusive and fair livelihood opportunities. It pertains to various types of changes, including but not limited to: Improved labour conditions Expanded employment opportunities Reduced barriers to entering markets (as businesses/enterprises) Strengthening the position of small scale producers in value chains Expanded access to markets (e.g. for nutritious foods, etc.)

description.narrative: This indicator measures the number of Internally Displaced People and refugees, including those living in camps, who receive appropriate forms of prereturn advice, support and counselling in order to equip them with knowledge, skills and attitudes needed for safe return. title.narrative: R8.3. Contributions to transformative policy changes (by sector, level, type and channel/modality)

description.narrative: Policies and institutions considered under this indicator may be either formal and informal and may correspond to changes from the national to the local (e.g. village) level. This indicator is primarily qualitative and is designed to adequately capture progress toward policy changes. For each area of contribution a narrative should be provided indicating what changes were supported, in what way they reflect a nexus approach, and the role of the NRM in contributing to these changes.Partners will need to monitor and report on their progress toward their policy objecives. Building alliances and networks Gaining support from decisionmakers Contributing to policy discussions Modifications to policiesAs this may often be a function of multiple partners in a single area/thematic programme, independent evaluation will subtantiate this.Policy changes that reflect the nexus approach are those that are multistakholder, multisectoral and multithematic, contextspecific and both conflict and gender sensitive.

title.narrative: R1.1. Number of persons receiving support related to sustainable livelihoods, secure employment, improved working conditions or professional/vocational and life skills

description.narrative: This indicator captures the number of individuals receiving support related to sustainable, inclusive and fair livelihood opportunities. It pertains to various types of changes, including but not limited to: Improved labour conditions Expanded employment opportunities Reduced barriers to entering markets (as businesses/enterprises) Strengthening the position of small scale producers in value chains Expanded access to markets (e.g. for nutritious foods, etc.)

title.narrative: R1.2. Number of persons involved in sustainable economic activities / employment as a result of NRM support. (disaggregated by sex)

description.narrative: This measures the total number of people supported throuugh NRM projects (directly or indirectly) who have either (1) improved an existing economic activity; (2) taken up a new one, whether related to primary production (agriculture), selfemployment (e.g. through a microenterprise) or through employment, or (3) been enabled to remain in employment/work during a crisis
